subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 76-year-old woman is brought to the clinic by her daughter because of 3 years of progressive memory loss and difficulty managing her finances. She scores 17/30 on the Mini-Mental State Examination, and brain MRI shows diffuse cortical atrophy with prominent hippocampal volume loss. At autopsy, extracellular cortical deposits are found that stain with Congo red and show apple-green birefringence under polarized light.
question: These deposits are best characterized by which of the following?

options.text: Alpha-helical aggregates of alpha-synuclein within neuronal cytoplasm
Paired helical filaments of hyperphosphorylated tau within neurons
Beta-pleated sheet-rich fibrils composed of amyloid beta peptide
Protease-resistant conformers of the prion protein

explanation_correct: The congophilic deposits with apple-green birefringence are amyloid, whose defining structural feature is a beta-pleated sheet conformation that binds Congo red. In Alzheimer disease the extracellular plaques are composed of amyloid beta peptide generated by cleavage of amyloid precursor protein (chromosome 21) by beta- and gamma-secretases. Misfolding of a normally soluble peptide into beta-sheet-rich fibrils is the shared mechanism of the amyloidoses.

explanation_incorrect.A: Alpha-synuclein aggregates are the hallmark of Parkinson disease and Lewy body dementia and are found within neurons rather than as extracellular plaques.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hyperphosphorylated tau forms intracellular neurofibrillary tangles, not the extracellular congophilic plaques described here.
explanation_incorrect.D: Prion protein conformers cause Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease and other spongiform encephalopathies; they are not the amyloid beta deposits of Alzheimer disease.
explanation_incorrect.E: Beta-2 microglobulin amyloidosis occurs in patients on long-term dialysis and deposits in joints and bone, not as cortical plaques.

educationalObjective: Amyloid deposits consist of beta-pleated sheet-rich protein fibrils that bind Congo red with apple-green birefringence, and in Alzheimer disease the extracellular plaques are made of amyloid beta peptide.
